content:
jamie: quick RFC follow-up — proposing a lightweight 'delta adapter' shim to ease v3 -> v4 API migration. idea is: small proxy that rewrites a few deprecated fields and does opt-in telemetry. minimal perf impact, easy rollback.
kevin: sounds promising. can you outline failure modes? esp around streaming and chunk boundaries.
jamie: sure — two main ones: 1) streaming framing mismatch (we'll forward EOF markers unchanged unless header present), 2) schema edgecases for nested choices (we'll add a safe-fallback mapping). both documented.
maria: what about security/tenant isolation? we can't let shim mutate sensitive payloads without an audit trail.
jamie: agreed. shim will run only in control plane we own for hosted customers, and for Dedicated/Private it's opt-in via feature flag + explicit consent. all mutations audited in trace.
sam: do we have a detection plan? how do we decide which requests hit shim automatically?
jamie: proposal: header-based detection + heuristic fallback. clients can send X-RW-Client-Version or X-RW-Compat; if missing we use a sniff (user-agent, body shape) but default is conservative (no mutation). example detector:

```
# pseudo
if req.headers.get("X-RW-Compat") == "v3":
  route_to("delta-adapter")
elif looks_like_v3(req.body):
  route_to("delta-adapter-heuristic")
else:
  route_to("v4")
```

kevin: we should avoid heuristic for first rollout. header-only for canary, then expand.
anya: telemetry note — please emit shim_metrics: shim_requests_total, shim_rewrites_total, shim_errors_total, shim_latency_ms and tag with tenant_id + detector_mode. need these for rollback SLOs.
jamie: yep will include. also plan to add a quality regression probe that runs golden prompt set against v3, shimmed v4, and native v4 and diff. automatic alerts if mismatch rate > 0.5%.
maria: rollout strategy?
jamie: staged: 1) internal-only — dev and staging (1 day), 2) canary tenants (5% opt-in header) for 48h, collect telemetry, 3) opt-in program for Dedicated customers (manual opt-in), 4) auto-opt for low-risk customers after 2 weeks and zero regressions. emergency kill switch exists.
sam: how to handle SDKs? we need a client-side opt-in toggle and a deprecation warning in SDKs for any older major versions. also emit a deprecation header: X-RW-Deprecation: v3; retry-after semantics if unsupported.
jeopardy-bot: deploy-bot: patch build passed: delta-adapter image pushed -> registry.redwood/internal/delta-adapter:2026-03-19-rc1 :white_check_mark:
ops-bot: Canaries started: 5% traffic to delta-adapter-canary group. monitor shim_errors_total > 0.05% to trigger rollback.
kevin: small nit — we need a mapping table for field rename rules. put that in config so we can hotfix without deploys. sample config:

```
field_mappings:
  old_choice -> choices
  top_level_input.text -> prompt
```

jamie: good call. config will be baked into k/v store with versioned keys.
maria: legal/compliance — ensure we log diffs but avoid storing PII. redact before audit log.
jamie: yes, diff logs will be hashed + redacted, raw payloads only kept if customer consents.
sam: ok when do we merge? we need RFC commit and a runbook.
jamie: i'll open a PR with runbook and the canary playbook after lunch. target merge Thu, deploy Fri morning to staging.
kevin: please add a step in runbook for verifying streaming behavior: send a 1-token-per-chunk stream and ensure no extra buffering introduced.
jamie: will add. thanks all — filing followups in the RFC thread and the runbook. :thumbsup:
